ja: だいさんじゅうごかい

p.src: Now Baochai had plainly heard Lin Daiyu's cutting remarks about her, but with her mother and brother weighing on her mind, she did not look back and went straight on her way. Lin Daiyu remained standing beneath the shade of the flowers, gazing from afar toward Happy Red Court. She watched Li Gongcai, Yingchun, Tanchun, Xichun, and all the others leave in groups after visiting the court, but still saw no sign of Xifeng. She wondered to herself, “Why has she not come to see Baoyu? Even if some business detained her, she would surely come to make a show of concern and win favor with the Old Lady and Lady Wang. There must be some reason why she has not come by this late hour.” While she was pondering this, she looked up again and saw a splendidly dressed throng approaching Happy Red Court. Looking closely, she saw Grandmother Jia leaning on Xifeng's arm, with Lady Xing and Lady Wang behind them, followed by Concubine Zhou, maids, married servants, and the rest, all entering the courtyard. At the sight, Daiyu could not help nodding. Thinking of the blessings enjoyed by those who still had parents, she was soon in tears again. A little later, she saw Baochai, Aunt Xue, and the others enter as well. Suddenly Zijuan came up from behind and said, “Miss, come and take your medicine. The boiled water has gone cold again.” Daiyu said, “What in the world do you want of me? All you do is pester me. What concern is it of yours whether I take it or not!” Zijuan laughed. “Your cough has only just improved a little, and already you are refusing your medicine again. Though it is the fifth month now and the weather is warm, you still ought to be careful. You have been standing half the morning in this damp place since early dawn. It is time you went back and rested.” Her words brought Daiyu to her senses, and only then did she notice that her legs were aching. After standing dazed for some time, she slowly took Zijuan's arm and returned to Bamboo Lodge.

p.src: As soon as she entered the courtyard, she saw the uneven shadows of bamboo spread across the ground and patches of moss in varying shades. She could not help recalling two lines from The Western Chamber: “In this secluded place, has anyone passed? White dew lies chill upon the spotted moss.” She sighed inwardly, “Shuangwen, Shuangwen, yours was truly an ill-starred fate. Yet unfortunate though you were, you still had a widowed mother and a young brother. Lin Daiyu, ill-fated as she is today, has neither widowed mother nor young brother. The ancients said, ‘Beauty is ever ill-fated’; but I am no beauty, so why should my fate be harsher even than Shuangwen's?” Absorbed in these thoughts, she walked on without heed. The parrot on the veranda saw Lin Daiyu coming and swooped down with a squawk, startling her. “You wretched creature!” she exclaimed. “You have showered my head with dust again.” The parrot flew back to its perch and cried, “Xueyan, lift the curtain quickly! Miss is here.” Daiyu stopped, tapped the perch with her hand, and asked, “Has its food and water been replenished?” The parrot heaved a long sigh remarkably like Daiyu's habitual sighing, then recited, “Today I bury flowers, and people laugh at my folly; when I am dead, who will bury me? See how, when spring is spent, the blossoms slowly fall: so too comes the hour when beauty ages and dies. Once spring is spent and beauty old, flowers fall and mortals die, each unaware of the other!” Daiyu and Zijuan both burst out laughing when they heard it. Zijuan said with a laugh, “Those are all verses you are always reciting, Miss. It is remarkable that the bird managed to remember them.” Daiyu had the perch taken down and hung instead from a hook outside the moon-shaped window. She then went indoors and sat by the inner side of the window. After taking her medicine, she saw the shadows of the bamboo outside cast upon the gauze. The whole room was filled with a dim, moist greenness, and even the bamboo matting felt cool. With nothing else to dispel her melancholy, Daiyu teased and played with the parrot through the gauze window and taught it to recite some of her favorite poems and songs. But we shall leave that aside for now.

p.src: Meanwhile, when Xue Baochai reached home, she found her mother doing her hair. The moment Aunt Xue saw her, she asked, “What brings you running here so early in the morning?” Baochai replied, “I came to see how you are feeling, Mother. After I left yesterday, I wondered whether he came back and made another scene.” As she spoke, she sat beside her mother and could no longer keep herself from weeping. When Aunt Xue saw her crying, she too lost control and wept for a while. At the same time she consoled her: “My child, do not feel so wronged. Just wait until I deal with him. If anything should happen to you, whom else would I have to depend upon?” Hearing them from outside, Xue Pan hurried in. Facing Baochai, he bowed again and again and kept saying, “Dear sister, forgive me just this once! The truth is, I had been drinking yesterday and came home late. I must have met with some evil influence on the road, and I was still not sober when I reached home. I have no idea what nonsense I said—I do not even know myself—so no wonder you are angry.” Baochai had been weeping with her face covered, but his words were so absurd that she could not help finding them amusing. She raised her head, spat toward the floor, and said, “There is no need to put on this pantomime. I know how much you resent the two of us, mother and daughter. You are trying every possible way to drive us away from you so that you may finally have some peace.” At this, Xue Pan hastily said with a smile, “Sister, where can such words have come from? If that is what you think, there is nowhere left for me to stand. You have never been one to imagine slights and say such perverse things.” Aunt Xue quickly added, “You notice only the unreasonable things your sister says. Do you mean to tell me that what you said last night was proper? You truly had taken leave of your senses!” Xue Pan said, “Mother, do not be angry, and Sister, do not distress yourself. What if, from now on, I promise never again to drink and roam about with that crowd?” Baochai laughed. “Now you are finally talking sense!” Aunt Xue said, “If you truly had that much determination, dragons would be laying eggs.” Xue Pan said, “If I ever go roaming with them again and Sister hears of it, she may spit at me as much as she likes and call me a beast and no man at all. How is that? Why should the two of you, all because of me alone, have to worry yourselves sick every day? It may be forgivable that Mother should grow angry because of me, but if I keep making Sister worry over me, then I am even less of a man. Now that Father is gone, instead of showing Mother greater filial devotion and cherishing my sister more, I make Mother angry and Sister miserable. Truly, I am worse than a beast.” As he spoke, he could no longer restrain himself, and tears rolled from his eyes. Aunt Xue had stopped crying, but his words stirred up her sorrow, and she began to weep again.

p.src: Forcing a smile, Baochai said, “You have made enough trouble, and now you have set Mother crying again.” Hearing this, Xue Pan hastily dried his tears and said with a smile, “When did I ever make Mother cry? Enough, enough, enough! Let us drop the matter and say no more about it. Call Xiangling in to pour some tea for your young mistress.” Baochai said, “I do not want any tea. As soon as Mother has washed her hands, we shall go over.” Xue Pan said, “Let me have a look at your necklet. I expect it is time to have it cleaned in the fire.” Baochai replied, “It is gleaming yellow already. Why have it cleaned again?” Xue Pan went on, “You ought to have some new clothes made now too. Tell me what colors and patterns you would like.” Baochai said, “I have not even worn all the clothes I already have. Why make more?” Presently Aunt Xue changed her clothes and took Baochai inside; only then did Xue Pan leave.

p.src: Meanwhile, Aunt Xue and Baochai entered the garden to visit Baoyu. When they reached Happy Red Court, they saw many maids and old serving-women standing both inside the side hall and along the outer covered corridors, and knew that Grandmother Jia and the others must all be there. Mother and daughter entered, exchanged greetings with everyone, and saw Baoyu lying on a couch. Aunt Xue asked whether he was feeling any better. Baoyu hurriedly tried to raise himself and answered, “A little better.” Then he added, “I am unworthy of all the trouble I have caused you and Cousin Baochai.” Aunt Xue quickly helped him lie down again and asked, “Whatever you want, you need only tell me.” Baoyu smiled. “If I think of anything, I shall certainly ask you for it.” Lady Wang asked, “What would you like to eat? We can have it sent to you presently.” Baoyu smiled. “There is nothing in particular I want, though that soup made once before with the tiny lotus leaves and little seedpods was rather good.” Xifeng laughed from beside him. “Listen to that! His taste is not exactly extravagant, only terribly troublesome. Of all things, he has set his heart on that.” Grandmother Jia at once repeatedly called for someone to go and make it. Xifeng laughed. “Do not be impatient, Old Ancestress. Let me think who has charge of the molds.” She turned and ordered an old serving-woman to ask the kitchen steward for them. The woman was gone a long while before returning to report, “The kitchen steward says all four sets of soup molds were handed back.” On hearing this, Xifeng thought for a moment and said, “I remember now whom I gave them to. They are most likely in the tea room.” She sent someone to ask the tea-room steward, but the molds had not been received there either. In the end, it was the keeper of the gold and silver vessels who brought them over.

p.src: Aunt Xue took them first and examined them. They proved to be a small case containing four sets of silver molds, each more than a foot long and about an inch square. Carved upon them were shapes the size of beans—chrysanthemums, plum blossoms, lotus seedpods, water-caltrops, and altogether thirty or forty different designs—all exquisitely wrought. She laughed and said to Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang, “Your household thinks of the most extraordinary things. Even a bowl of soup has to be made in all these shapes! If you had not told me, I would never have guessed what these were used for.” Without waiting for anyone else to speak, Xifeng laughed and said, “How could you know, Aunt? This was an idea they devised when preparing a meal last year. They press some sort of dough into these shapes, borrow a little fragrance from fresh lotus leaves, and rely entirely on a good broth. In the end there is nothing much to it, and no household would eat it regularly. They made it just once as a sample. I wonder what made him think of it today.” As she spoke, she took the case and handed it to a woman, instructing the kitchen to take several chickens at once, add other ingredients, and make a dozen or so bowls. Lady Wang asked, “Why make so much?” Xifeng laughed. “There is a reason. This is not something we ordinarily make. Since Brother Baoyu has asked for it today, it would hardly seem right to prepare it for him alone while the Old Lady, Aunt Xue, and you had none. We may as well seize the chance to make enough for everyone, and then, thanks to him, I shall get to share in the treat too.” Grandmother Jia laughed when she heard this. “You little monkey, how clever you are! You use the household’s money to win yourself favor.” At this, everyone laughed. Xifeng also hastened to laugh. “That makes no difference. I can still afford to offer this little treat as my mark of respect.” She turned and instructed the woman, “Tell the kitchen to use plenty of good ingredients and prepare it properly. They may charge the silver to my account.” The woman acknowledged the order and left.

p.src: Baochai laughed from the side. “I have been here for several years now, and from what I have carefully observed, however clever that girl Feng may be, she can never outdo Grandmother.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia replied, “I am old now. What cleverness can I still claim? When I was Feng’s age, I was cleverer still. Though she may not equal us, she is good enough as she is and far more capable than your aunt. Your poor aunt hardly ever speaks and is as wooden as a block, so she does not show to much advantage before her parents-in-law. Feng has such a winning tongue—how could anyone blame people for loving her?” Baoyu laughed. “If that is so, are those who speak little not loved?” Grandmother Jia said, “Those who speak little have their own lovable qualities, while clever talkers have their objectionable side too. In fact, it is better to say nothing.” Baoyu laughed. “Exactly. I was thinking that although my elder sister-in-law says little, Grandmother treats her just as affectionately as Cousin Feng. If only those with clever tongues were lovable, then among all these sisters only Cousin Feng and Cousin Lin would deserve to be loved.” Grandmother Jia said, “Speaking of the girls—and I do not say this merely to flatter your aunt in her presence—it is perfectly true that none of the four girls in our family can compare with Baochai.” Aunt Xue hastily laughed. “Your Ladyship is being partial in saying that.” Lady Wang also quickly said with a smile, “Her Ladyship often praises Baochai to me in private, so those are no empty words.” Baoyu had prompted Grandmother Jia in the hope that she would praise Lin Daiyu, and was quite taken aback when she praised Baochai instead. He looked at Baochai and smiled. But Baochai had already turned away to speak with Xiren. Just then someone came to summon them to the meal. Grandmother Jia rose, told Baoyu to take good care of himself, and repeated her instructions to the maids. Then, leaning on Xifeng and courteously yielding precedence to Aunt Xue, she left the room with the others. She asked whether the soup was ready, then said to Aunt Xue and the others, “Whatever you feel like eating, just tell me. I know how to make that girl Feng procure it for us.” Aunt Xue laughed. “Your Ladyship does know how to tease her. She is forever preparing delicacies to show her devotion, yet you can never eat very much of them.” Xifeng laughed. “Please do not say that, Aunt. Our venerable ancestress merely finds human flesh too sour. If she did not, she would have eaten me long ago.”

p.src: Before she had even finished, Grandmother Jia and all the others burst into loud laughter. Even Baoyu, inside his room, could not keep from laughing. Xiren laughed. “Second Mistress’s tongue is truly enough to frighten one to death!” Baoyu reached out, took Xiren’s hand, and asked with a smile, “You have been standing all this time. Are you tired?” As he spoke, he drew her down to sit beside him. Xiren laughed. “You have forgotten again. While Miss Bao is still in the courtyard, ask her to have Yinger come and make a few cords for you.” Baoyu laughed. “It is lucky you reminded me.” Then he raised his head toward the window and called, “Sister Bao, after dinner, would you ask Yinger to come and make a few cords for me? Will she have the time?” Hearing him, Baochai turned and replied, “Why should she not? I shall send her over presently.” Grandmother Jia and the others had not heard clearly, so they stopped and asked Baochai what had been said. Once Baochai explained, they all understood. Grandmother Jia added, “Good child, have her make a few for your brother. If that leaves you with no one to attend you, I have plenty of idle maids. Choose whichever one you like and take her into your service.” Aunt Xue, Baochai, and the others all laughed. “Just send her over to make them. There will be no need for anyone to attend us. She has nothing to do all day but idle about and make mischief.”

Aunt Xue, Baochai, and the others all laughed. “Just send her over to make them. There will be no need for anyone to attend us.
She has nothing to do all day but idle about and make mischief.”

p.src: Still talking, they walked on and suddenly saw Shi Xiangyun, Pinger, Xiangling, and several others picking balsam flowers beside the rockery. When the girls saw them approaching, they all came forward to meet them. Before long they reached the garden gate. Lady Wang, fearing that Grandmother Jia was tired, proposed that she rest for a while in the main apartments. Grandmother Jia’s legs were indeed aching, so she nodded her assent. Lady Wang immediately ordered a maid to hurry ahead and arrange the seats. At the time, Concubine Zhao had pleaded illness, so only Concubine Zhou and the serving women and maids were there, bustling about to raise the curtains, set out backrests, and spread cushions. Supported by Xifeng, Grandmother Jia entered and took the host’s seat opposite Aunt Xue, who sat as the guest. Xue Baochai and Shi Xiangyun sat below them. Lady Wang personally presented tea to Grandmother Jia, while Li Gongcai served Aunt Xue. Grandmother Jia said to Lady Wang, “Let the younger daughters-in-law wait upon us. Sit down over there so that we may talk.” Only then did Lady Wang sit on a small stool. She instructed Xifeng, “Her Ladyship will dine here. Have some additional dishes brought in.” Xifeng acknowledged the order and went out. She sent someone to notify the servants in Grandmother Jia’s quarters; the serving women there hastily passed the word along, and all the maids hurried over. Lady Wang then ordered someone to “invite the young ladies.” After they had been summoned for some time, only Tanchun and Xichun appeared. Yingchun was feeling unwell and would not dine, while Lin Daiyu went without saying: ordinarily she ate properly at only five meals out of ten, so no one paid much attention. Presently the meal arrived, and the servants set the tables in place. Xifeng stood below, holding a bundle of ivory chopsticks wrapped in a napkin, and said with a smile, “Ancestress and Aunt need not stand on ceremony. Just do as I tell you.” Grandmother Jia smiled at Aunt Xue. “This is how we always do things.” Aunt Xue assented with a smile. Xifeng then set out four pairs: the two at the head were for Grandmother Jia and Aunt Xue, while those on either side were for Xue Baochai and Shi Xiangyun. Lady Wang, Li Gongcai, and the others remained standing below, watching as the dishes were served. Xifeng first busied herself with having clean utensils brought so that she could choose some dishes for Baoyu.

p.src: Before long, the lotus-leaf soup arrived, and Grandmother Jia inspected it. Lady Wang turned and saw Yuchuan nearby, so she ordered her to take it to Baoyu. Xifeng said, “She cannot carry it all by herself.” As luck would have it, Ying’er and Xi’er both arrived just then. Baochai knew that they had already eaten, so she said to Ying’er, “Brother Bao has been asking you to make a net for him. You two may go together.” Ying’er assented and went out with Yuchuan. Ying’er said, “It is such a long way, and terribly hot besides. How are we to carry all this there?” Yuchuan laughed. “Don’t worry. I have a way.” With that, she summoned an old serving woman, put the soup, rice, and other dishes into a covered carrying box, and had the woman bear it behind them while the two girls walked empty-handed. Only after they had passed through the gate of Happy Red Court did Yuchuan take the box herself, and she and Ying’er entered Baoyu’s room. Xiren, Sheyue, and Qiuwen were laughing and joking with Baoyu. When they saw the two girls arrive, they all hurried to their feet and said with a laugh, “What perfect timing! How did the two of you happen to come together?” As they spoke, they took the things from them. Yuchuan sat down on a low stool, but Ying’er did not dare to take a seat. Xiren hurriedly brought her a footstool, but still Ying’er did not dare sit down. Baoyu was delighted to see Ying’er, but when he suddenly noticed Yuchuan, he thought of her elder sister Jinchuan. Overcome with grief and shame, he neglected Ying’er and spoke to Yuchuan instead. Seeing Ying’er ignored, Xiren feared that she might feel awkward; and since she still refused to sit, Xiren took her by the hand and led her to another room for tea and conversation.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sheyue and the others laid out bowls and chopsticks and prepared to serve Baoyu his meal. Baoyu would not eat, but asked Yuchuan, “Is your mother well?” Her face full of anger, Yuchuan would not even look directly at him. Only after a long silence did she answer with a single word: “Yes.” Baoyu felt rebuffed. After another long pause, he had no choice but to smile ingratiatingly and ask, “Who told you to bring this to me?” “Who else but the mistresses and ladies?” replied Yuchuan. Seeing her still so sullen, Baoyu understood that it was because of Jinchuan. He wanted to humble himself and coax her around, but with so many people present he could not bring himself to do so. He therefore tried every means to send them all away, then smiled ingratiatingly again and plied her with solicitous questions. Though Yuchuan had been displeased at first, she saw that Baoyu never once lost his temper. No matter how sharply she taunted him, he remained gentle and good-natured. At last she herself began to feel embarrassed, and a trace of cheer returned to her face. Baoyu smiled and pleaded, “Dear sister, bring me that soup and let me taste it.” Yuchuan replied, “I have never learned to feed anyone. Wait until the others return before you eat.” Baoyu laughed. “I’m not asking you to feed me. I cannot walk, so if you hand it to me and let me eat, you can go back early, report that your errand is done, and have your own meal. If I keep delaying you like this, won’t you go hungry? If you cannot be bothered to move, I shall simply have to endure the pain and get down to fetch it myself.” As he spoke, he made to get out of bed; but when he struggled to rise, he could not suppress a cry of pain. Unable to bear seeing him like this, Yuchuan rose and said, “Lie down! What evil karma you must have created in a former life to suffer its retribution now! How could I possibly stand by and watch you with either of my eyes?” Even as she spoke, she burst into a little laugh and brought the soup over. Baoyu smiled. “Dear sister, be as angry as you like while you are here, but when you see Grandmother and Mother, do try to look a little more pleasant. If you carry on like this, you will only be scolded again.” “Eat, then! Go on, eat!” said Yuchuan. “There is no need to butter me up with sweet words. I don’t believe any of that!” With that, she urged Baoyu to drink two mouthfuls of soup. Baoyu deliberately said, “It doesn’t taste good. I won’t have any more.” Yuchuan exclaimed, “Amitabha! If even this is not good, what would you call good?” “It has no flavor at all,” said Baoyu. “If you don’t believe me, taste it yourself and you’ll see.” Yuchuan, piqued by his words, actually took a taste. Baoyu laughed. “Now it tastes good.” Only then did Yuchuan realize that Baoyu had tricked her into taking a mouthful. She said, “Since you said it tasted bad, I won’t give you any now, even if you say it tastes good.”

p.src: Just as the maid came in, someone suddenly arrived to report, “Two of Second Master Fu’s old nurses have come to pay their respects and see Second Master Bao.” At this, Baoyu knew that they were old nurses from the household of Fu Shi, the assistant prefect. Fu Shi had originally been one of Jia Zheng’s protégés. Over the years he had prospered by relying on the Jia family’s prestige and influence, while Jia Zheng also held him in genuine regard. He was therefore treated differently from the other protégés and often sent members of his household to maintain relations. Baoyu ordinarily detested foolish men and dull-witted women above all else, so why did he now have the two old women shown in? There was, in fact, a reason. Baoyu had heard that Fu Shi had a younger sister named Fu Qiufang, a rare jewel among secluded maidens, who was often said to possess both talent and beauty. Though he had never seen her himself, he cherished a distant admiration for her with the utmost reverence. Fearing that refusing the women admission might slight Fu Qiufang, he hastily ordered that they be shown in. Fu Shi was a parvenu. Since Fu Qiufang possessed some beauty and exceptional intelligence, he was determined to use his sister to secure a marriage alliance with a great and noble family and would not lightly promise her to anyone; hence her marriage had been delayed until now. Fu Qiufang was now twenty-three years old and still unbetrothed. Unfortunately, the great and noble families looked down on Fu Shi as a penniless pedant of shallow roots and were unwilling to seek the match. Fu Shi’s close association with the Jia family was itself motivated by a private design. As it happened, the two old women he had sent that day were exceedingly ignorant. Hearing that Baoyu wished to see them, they came in, had scarcely finished their greetings, and exchanged no more than a few words with him. Seeing strangers arrive, Yuchuan ceased teasing Baoyu and merely stood holding the soup and listening to the conversation. Baoyu, absorbed in talking with the old women, continued eating while reaching out for the soup. Both of them had their eyes on the visitors. Baoyu unexpectedly thrust out his hand too forcefully, knocking the bowl over and spilling the soup onto it. Yuchuan had not been scalded, but she started in fright and hurriedly laughed, “Goodness, what has happened!” The alarmed maids hurried forward to take the bowl. Baoyu seemed not to notice that his own hand had been scalded and kept asking Yuchuan, “Where were you scalded? Does it hurt?” Yuchuan and everyone else burst out laughing. Yuchuan said, “You are the one who was scalded, yet you keep asking about me.” Only on hearing this did Baoyu realize that he himself had been scalded. Everyone hurried forward to put things in order. Baoyu stopped eating, washed his hands, drank some tea, and exchanged another few words with the two old women. The two old women then took their leave. Qingwen and the others escorted them as far as the bridge before returning.

p.src: Once the two old women saw that no one was around, they began talking as they walked. One laughed and said, “No wonder people say that their Baoyu is fine enough on the outside but muddle-headed within—pleasant to look at but of no practical use. He really is rather foolish. He scalded his own hand, yet asked someone else whether she was hurt. If that does not make him a fool, what does?” The other laughed as well. “The last time I came, I heard many people in his household complaining about him. It is absolutely true that he is rather foolish. Though drenched by the downpour like a half-drowned fowl, he went about telling others, ‘It is raining—hurry and take shelter.’ Is that not ridiculous? Often, when no one is near, he weeps and laughs by himself. If he sees swallows, he talks to the swallows; if he sees fish in the river, he talks to the fish. When he looks upon the stars and moon, he either sighs endlessly or mutters under his breath. What is more, he has not the least firmness in him and even submits to the temper of those little slipshod maids. When the mood takes him to cherish things, he considers even a loose end of thread precious; but when the mood takes him to squander them, he cares nothing even for objects worth thousands or tens of thousands.” Still talking, the two women walked out of the garden, bade everyone farewell, and returned home. There is no more to say of them.

p.src: Now, after the visitors had gone, Xiren brought Ying’er over and asked Baoyu what sort of cords he wanted knotted. Baoyu smiled at Ying’er. “I was so absorbed in talking just now that I forgot all about you. I troubled you to come for no other reason than to knot several cords for me.” Ying’er asked, “Cords for holding what?” At this question Baoyu smiled and said, “Whatever they might hold, make me several of every kind.” Ying’er clapped her hands and laughed. “Goodness gracious! If you want that, I could not finish them in ten years.” Baoyu laughed. “Dear sister, you have nothing else to do when you are free, so make them all for me.” Xiren laughed. “How could she finish them all at once? For now, let her choose two of the more necessary ones.” Ying’er said, “What is necessary? There are only fans, perfume pendants, and waist-sashes.” “A waist-sash will do,” said Baoyu. Ying’er asked, “What color is the sash?” Baoyu said, “Bright red.” Ying’er said, “With bright red, a black cord looks best; or a deep blue one would be strong enough to balance the color.” Baoyu asked, “What goes with pine-pollen yellow?” Ying’er replied, “Pine-pollen yellow goes with peach-pink.” Baoyu laughed. “Now that is delicate and vivid. I also want something understated and elegant, yet touched with brightness.” Ying’er said, “Scallion green and willow yellow are my favorite pairing.” Baoyu said, “Very well. Make one in peach-pink and another in scallion green.” Ying’er asked, “What pattern would you like?” Baoyu asked, “How many patterns are there altogether?” Ying’er replied, “Single Incense Stick, Upturned Stool, Elephant-Eye Lozenge, Double Diamond, Linked Rings, Plum Blossom, and Willow Leaf.” Baoyu asked, “What was the pattern you made for Third Miss the other day?” Ying’er replied, “That was the Clustered-Heart Plum Blossom.” Baoyu said, “That pattern will do nicely.” As they spoke, Baoyu had just asked Xiren to fetch the thread when an old woman outside the window announced that the young ladies’ meal was ready. Baoyu said, “Go and eat. Finish quickly and come back.” Xiren laughed. “We have a guest here. How could we possibly leave to eat?” While sorting the threads, Ying’er laughed and said, “Why ever should you say that? Do be sensible and hurry off to eat.” Only then did Xiren and the others leave, keeping behind two young maids to answer any summons.

p.src: As Baoyu watched Ying'er knotting the net, he chatted idly with her and asked, “How old are you?” Continuing to work with her hands, Ying'er replied, “Sixteen.” Baoyu asked, “What is your family name?” “Huang,” said Ying'er. Baoyu laughed. “Then your full name suits you perfectly—you really are a little golden oriole.” Ying'er laughed. “My given name originally had two characters: Jinying, ‘Golden Oriole.’ My young mistress thought it awkward to say, so she shortened it to Ying'er, and now everyone calls me that.” Baoyu said, “Cousin Bao certainly treats you kindly. When she marries someday, you will surely go with her.” Ying'er pursed her lips in a smile. Baoyu laughed. “I often say to Xiren, ‘I wonder what fortunate man will one day have the joy of possessing both mistress and maid.’” Ying'er laughed. “You still don't know how many virtues our young mistress has that no one else in the world possesses. Her looks are the least of them.” Ying'er's charming innocence, her lilting voice, and her artless smiles had already captivated Baoyu; how much more stirred was he when she began to speak of Baochai! He therefore asked her, “What are those virtues? Dear sister, tell me all about them.” Ying'er laughed. “I'll tell you, but you must promise not to repeat it to her.” “Of course not,” Baoyu replied with a laugh. Just then, a voice outside exclaimed, “Why is it so quiet in here?” They turned to look, and the newcomer was none other than Baochai. Baoyu hurriedly offered her a seat. After sitting down, Baochai asked Ying'er, “What are you making?” As she spoke, she looked at the work in Ying'er's hands; it was only half finished. Baochai laughed. “What interest is there in that? You might as well make a net for the jade pendant instead.” Her words reminded Baoyu, and he clapped his hands and laughed. “You are quite right, cousin. I had forgotten all about it. But what color would go best with it?” Baochai replied, “Mixed colors certainly would not do. Bright red would clash with its color, yellow would not stand out, and black would be too somber. Let me think of a way: bring the gold thread and ply it strand by strand with black beaded thread. A net knotted from those would look splendid.”

u.src: As Baoyu watched Ying'er knotting the net, he chatted idly with her and asked, “How old are you?”
Continuing to work with her hands, Ying'er replied, “Sixteen.”
Baoyu asked, “What is your family name?”
“Huang,” said Ying'er.
Baoyu laughed. “Then your full name suits you perfectly—you really are a little golden oriole.”
Ying'er laughed. “My given name originally had two characters: Jinying, ‘Golden Oriole.’
My young mistress thought it awkward to say, so she shortened it to Ying'er, and now everyone calls me that.”
Baoyu said, “Cousin Bao certainly treats you kindly.
When she marries someday, you will surely go with her.”
Ying'er pursed her lips in a smile.
Baoyu laughed. “I often say to Xiren, ‘I wonder what fortunate man will one day have the joy of possessing both mistress and maid.’”
Ying'er laughed. “You still don't know how many virtues our young mistress has that no one else in the world possesses. Her looks are the least of them.”
Ying'er's charming innocence, her lilting voice, and her artless smiles had already captivated Baoyu; how much more stirred was he when she began to speak of Baochai!
He therefore asked her, “What are those virtues?
Dear sister, tell me all about them.”
Ying'er laughed. “I'll tell you, but you must promise not to repeat it to her.”
“Of course not,” Baoyu replied with a laugh.
Just then, a voice outside exclaimed, “Why is it so quiet in here?”
They turned to look, and the newcomer was none other than Baochai.
Baoyu hurriedly offered her a seat.
After sitting down, Baochai asked Ying'er, “What are you making?”
As she spoke, she looked at the work in Ying'er's hands; it was only half finished.
Baochai laughed. “What interest is there in that? You might as well make a net for the jade pendant instead.”
Her words reminded Baoyu, and he clapped his hands and laughed. “You are quite right, cousin. I had forgotten all about it.
But what color would go best with it?”
Baochai replied, “Mixed colors certainly would not do. Bright red would clash with its color, yellow would not stand out, and black would be too somber.
Let me think of a way: bring the gold thread and ply it strand by strand with black beaded thread. A net knotted from those would look splendid.”

p.src: Baoyu was delighted by the suggestion and repeatedly called for Xiren to fetch the gold thread. Just then Xiren came in carrying two bowls of food and told Baoyu, “Something strange happened today. A little while ago, Madam sent someone to bring me these two bowls of food.” Baoyu laughed. “There must have been extra dishes today, so she sent them for all of you to share.” “No,” said Xiren. “She specified that they were for me, yet did not even require me to go and kowtow in thanks. That is what makes it so strange.” Baochai laughed. “If they were given to you, just eat them. What is there to wonder about?” Xiren smiled. “Nothing like this has ever happened before. It makes me feel quite embarrassed.” Baochai pursed her lips in a smile. “Does this embarrass you already? Someday there will be something that embarrasses you even more.” Xiren perceived a deeper meaning in her words. Knowing that Baochai was not given to flippant mockery, she recalled Madam Wang's intentions the other day and said no more. Showing the dishes to Baoyu, she said, “Wash your hands, and then come and get the thread.” With that, she went straight out. After the meal, she washed her hands and returned with the gold thread to knot the net with Ying'er. By then, Baochai had already been summoned away by a messenger from Xue Pan.

p.src: While Baoyu was watching the net being knotted, two maids suddenly arrived from Lady Xing with two kinds of fruit for him. They asked, “Are you able to walk yet? If you can get about, she asks that you come over tomorrow to take your mind off things. Madam is truly very concerned about you.” Baoyu hurriedly replied, “As soon as I am able to walk, I shall certainly go and pay my respects to Madam. The pain is less severe than before. Please tell her not to worry.” As he invited the two maids to sit down, he called Qiuwen and told her to take half of the newly arrived fruit to Miss Lin. Qiuwen assented and was just about to leave when Daiyu's voice was heard in the courtyard. Baoyu hurriedly called, “Invite her in at once!” To learn what followed, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
